high_cpu.title: High CPU utilisation
steps: Confirm the alarm is sustained, not a brief spike (check 15-minute average, not one datapoint).
Check for a stuck retry loop or a deploy that landed without the expected autoscaling policy.
Scale out (increase desired count) before scaling up; cheaper and faster to reverse.
If a single task/instance is the outlier, replace it rather than restarting in place.

error_rate.title: Elevated error rate
steps: Pull the last 15 minutes of application logs for the affected service and group by error message.
Check the most recent deploy timestamp against when the error rate started climbing.
If tied to a deploy, roll back first and investigate second -- restoring service comes before root cause.
If not tied to a deploy, check a dependency (database, downstream API) for its own alarms.

proposed_action.description: Enable the checkout-api-test maintenance-mode flag to shed load onto a degraded-but-safe path while the error rate is investigated. Safe and reversible: set back to "false" once resolved (Tier 2's rollback step does exactly this and verifies it).
proposed_action.risk: low -- a feature flag read by the (synthetic) service, not a destructive action; requires human approval and is enforced by an AgentCore Gateway Cedar policy, not executed directly by this agent.

latency.title: Elevated latency
steps: Check whether latency correlates with a traffic spike (likely capacity) or is flat-rate (likely a dependency).
Look for a downstream service's own latency/error alarms before assuming the local service is at fault.
If capacity-bound, scale out; if dependency-bound, consider a circuit breaker or cached fallback.

default.title: Unclassified finding
steps: No runbook matched this finding's keywords. Escalate to a human on-call with the raw finding text.
Do not take an automated remediation action on an unclassified finding.
